body.x: Passwords can be stolen and a face can be copied from a photo, so the search is on for something no one else can present. A pattern of brain activity is about as personal as it gets.
YNEURO was named a 2027 Honoree in Cybersecurity and Enterprise Tech at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for Neuro ID, a neural-signature authentication technology.

Neuro ID is an authentication technology that verifies a person's identity through their unique neural signature. Non-invasive EEG sensors embedded in a wearable capture the user's neural activity, and machine-learning models analyze the signals and match them against the enrolled signature, confirming identity the moment the device is worn and continuously while it stays on.

The technology has been demonstrated publicly, with users enrolling and authenticating in real time. Unlike passwords, nothing needs to be typed or remembered, and unlike fingerprints or faces, the neural signature is not externally visible and cannot be captured at a distance.

Delivered as embedded software and licensed to device and wearable makers for integration into smart glasses, earbuds and headsets, it enables device unlock, secure payments and access to protected accounts and systems for consumer, enterprise and government use.

The CES Innovation Awards program, an annual competition honoring outstanding design and engineering in consumer technology products, recognizes all recipients as Honorees at two levels. The Honoree level covers products that score above the scoring threshold in each category, while Best of Innovation goes to the highest-scoring Honorees. A panel of industry expert judges and global media scores each product on engineering and functionality, aesthetic and design, and what makes it unique and innovative.

At CES 2027, AVING NEWS will operate the AVING TECH TALK broadcast zone at the Venetian Expo (Hall A, Booth 50271), providing on-site coverage and interviews that spotlight Korean companies and their latest innovations.

Ahead of CES 2027, AVING NEWS will host the 3rd Innovation Awards Winners Networking Party at MIK BASE CAMP on Wednesday, November 25, at 5 p.m. The event will also feature individual video interviews with participating companies, with registration available through Eventus. In early December, AVING NEWS will begin its pre-show coverage, including an interview program connecting Korean innovators with U.S. media outlets that regularly cover CES and participate in the Innovation Awards judging process.
